source_title: J. Crew Files Bankruptcy, Felled by Pandemic and Heavy Debt
company_context: J.Crew Group Inc., a US apparel retailer, was acquired in a 2011 leveraged buyout by TPG Capital and Leonard Green & Partners in a roughly $3 billion deal. The LBO transformed a near-debt-free balance sheet into a heavily leveraged one. J.Crew filed for Chapter 11 on May 4, 2020 as the COVID-19 pandemic closed stores, becoming one of the first major retail bankruptcies of the pandemic.
business_type: Brick-and-mortar and catalog apparel retail (specialty preppy clothing, including Madewell brand)
evidence_summary: J.Crew filed Chapter 11 on May 4, 2020, crushed by debt rooted in its 2011 LBO and pushed over the edge by pandemic store closures. The company had about $50 million of long-term debt in 2010 before the buyout was announced; by February 1, 2020 it carried roughly $1.7 billion. As part of the prearranged restructuring, lenders agreed to convert about $1.65 billion of debt into equity, taking control of the company, and J.Crew lined up $400 million in financing to operate during the case.

source_backed_metrics.lbo_deal_value_2011_usd: approximately $3 billion (TPG Capital and Leonard Green & Partners)

outcome_evidence: Filed Chapter 11 on May 4, 2020 with a prearranged deal: lenders converted ~$1.65 billion of debt to equity and took control; $400 million in financing arranged to operate through the case.
source_limitations: Named journalism summary; underlying court docket not fetched directly. Figures as-reported and rounded; debt growth from ~$50 million (2010) to ~$1.7 billion (2020) reflects the LBO leverage, corroborated across multiple outlets.
directly_stated: Acquired in 2011 LBO by TPG Capital and Leonard Green & Partners (~$3 billion)
Long-term debt ~$50 million in 2010 vs ~$1.7 billion as of Feb 1, 2020
Lenders agreed to convert ~$1.65 billion of debt into equity
$400 million financing arranged for the bankruptcy
inferred: The LBO-installed debt removed the resilience needed to survive a demand shock
Pandemic store closures were the trigger, not the root cause, of insolvency
why_useful_for_opsiq: A pairing of LBO debt_solvency_pressure with a demand shock, where the visible trigger (pandemic) masks the structural cause (leverage). The before/after debt figures (~$50M to ~$1.7B) make it ideal for testing whether OpsIQ attributes failure to the correct dimension rather than the most recent event.
